sentences.text: Trishala Sharma vs Shailender Bhardwaj on 13 March, 2024

Bench: Pankaj Mithal, Prashant Kumar Mishra
 In The Supreme Court Of India
 Civil Original Jurisdiction
 Transfer Petition (Civil ) No. 288 Of 2023
 Trishala Sharma ... Pet
 Versus
 Shailender Bhardwaj ... Res
 O R D E R
In this transfer petition, the parties were referred to the Mediation Centre where a settlement has been arrived at between the parties to 17th October, 2023.
The settlement is on record and is admitted to the parties.
2. According, to the settlement, the parties have decided to divorce each other and to live separately.

The husband has agreed to pay a total sum of Rs. 10,00,000/-
(Rupees Ten Lakhs only) in two equal installments in full and final settlement.

3. The terms and conditions of the settlement reads as under :-
 XXXXX XXXXX XXXXX XXXXX Comprehensive mediation sessions were held with the parties separately and jointly on 11.08.2023, 01.09.2023, 05.09.2023, 20.09.2023, 05.10.2023, 09.10.2023 and today i.e. on 17.10.2023 and with the indulgence of counsels and Mediator, the parties have Reason: arrived at an amicable settlement on the following terms and conditions:
1. Both the parties hereto confirm and declare that they have voluntarily and of their own free-will, decided not to live together as husband and wife and seek divorce by way of mutual consent.
They have arrived at this Settlement in the presence of the mediator, their respective counsels.

2. That the following cases are pending between the parties:-

1

sentences.text: 3. That both the parties have entered into a full and final settlement / agreement in respect to the above mentioned cases on the following terms & conditions:

(i) It has been agreed between both the parties that Respondent-husband / Mr.
Shailender Bhardwaj, shall pay a sum of Rs. 10,00,000/-
(Rupees Ten Lakhs Only) by way Demand Draft/RTGS towards her Stridhan, maintenance past,
present, future and permanent Alimony and any other claims criminal or civil in nature.

The mode of payment is as under:-
(ii) The first installment of Rs. 5,00,000/-
(Rupees Five Lakh Only) will be paid by the Respondent husband to the Petitioner wife on or before 17th December 2023.
(iii) The parties are free to jointly move application under Article 142 before Supreme Court of India after the payment of 1st installment on or before 17.12.2023 and not later than 28.02.2024 before the payment of the second installment.
(iv) The full and final second installment payment of Rs. 5,00,000/- (Rupees Five Lakh Only) to the Petitioner wife by the Respondent husband will be paid on or before 28.02.2024.
4. That both the parties herein agree that all the pending cases whether specifically mentioned or not between the parties & their family members arising out of the present matrimonial dispute herein shall be withdrawn.
The parties and / or their family members, relatives or representatives undertake not to initiate any other litigation against each other in future also.
Both the parties will co-operate with each other for quashing / withdrawn of case pending between the parties and their family members or their relatives.

Trishala Sharma vs Shailender Bhardwaj on 13 March, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/105023402/
2 5.

That both the parties have agreed that none of them will make any effort to defame / malign the other party in person or their respective parents or relatives through any social media or forum in any other manner.

6. Both the parties agree and undertake that they have settled all their disputes and grievances against each other and against their family members amicably and they shall not file any complaints, proceedings whether criminal or civil, if any against each other or their family members or stake any claim on the movable or immovable, joint or ancestral, self- acquired or HUF properties of either parties and their respective families.
Both the parties further undertake to withdraw the aforesaid matters or any other matter if any pending against each other anywhere.

7. By signing this Agreement, the parties hereto solemnly state and affirm that they have no further claims or demands against each other and all the disputes and differences have been amicably settled by the parties hereto, through the process of Mediation.

8. That both the parties agree and undertake that they have settled all their disputes and grievances against each other and against their family members amicably in terms of the present settlement agreement and have agreed to remain bound by the terms and conditions as have been mutually and amicably agreed by the parties herein.
9. That the parties are accordingly signing this settlement agreement in presence of all named above, to authenticate their will to comply the same as agreed above.

4. In view of the aforesaid facts and circumstances and looking to fact that marriage between the parties have broken down irretrievably and they have decided to part ways as per the settlement, we consider it to be a fit case for exercising powers under Article 142 of the Constitution of India.
Accordingly, the marriage between the parties solemnized on 4th February, 2021 at Delhi is dissolved in terms of the Settlement Deed dated 17 th October, 2023 which shall form part of this order.

5. Needless to say, that the parties shall abide by the terms and conditions of the Settlement Agreement.
6. In view of the above facts, the IA No. 62545/2024 is allowed.
7. The transfer petition and pending application(s), shall stand disposed of.
. .J. [PANKAJ MITHAL] .

.J. 
[PRASHANT KUMAR MISHRA]
